title: Collaboration: Authorize Channel Reads and Sends
businessContext: A guessed private-channel ID lets an authenticated user read another team’s messages. Archived channels also accept new sends.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ tenantId, channel, session, members, action }). channel has id, tenantId, private and archived booleans. session is null or { userId, tenantId, active }. members contains unique users with { userId, role:member|admin, active }. action outside read/send/manage => invalid_action first. Missing/inactive session or empty userId => unauthenticated. Session or channel tenant mismatch => forbidden. Private channels require active membership; manage always requires an active admin membership, including public channels. Fail these checks as forbidden. An authorized send to an archived channel => read_only. Otherwise allow. Return { allowed, reason } with reason allowed for success. Inputs otherwise have valid shapes.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would you revoke an active socket subscription immediately when channel membership changes?

testCases.name: Read a public channel as active tenant user
Deny cross-tenant session even with membership
Deny inactive membership in private channel
Public channel management still requires admin
Active admin can manage archived private channel
Reject unknown action before missing session

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
